newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Foreign investment in Honduras jumps in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Honduras jumps in 1996.

text.p: Foreign investment in Honduras reached $837.5 million in 1996, way up from $475 million in 1995, the Industry, Commerce and Tourism Ministry said on Tuesday.
Of the 1996 total, $620 million came from the United States compared to $375 million in 1995, the ministry said.

"This increase in foreign investment in Honduras shows that there is a favorable climate in our country for business, and we hope that this trend continues," Minister Fernando Garcia said in a statement.
The report did not break out which sectors received the foreign cash.
After the United States, El Salvador was the biggest investor in Honduras with $50 million, up from $35.5 million in 1995, the ministry said.
South Korea followed with $35 million and Hong Kong and Taiwan were next with $30 million each.
Most of the Asian investment is believed to be in so-called "maquiladora" industries, in which textiles are sewn into clothes by cheap labor and exported to the United States and other countries.
Britain accounted for $20 million in investment, Guatemala $5.5 million and Spain, Venezuela and Costa Rica $5 million each.
The amount invested increased from each country except Spain, which poured $20 million into Honduras in 1995.
